speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with a limp and localized pain, and I note you have no fever or acute distress. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and what activity makes it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The child is a 7-year-old male with a limp and pain localized to the left knee, favoring that leg during activity, without fever or trauma. Since the pain is referred to the knee, where is the actual tenderness or swelling located in the joint or surrounding area?

REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, CBC

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease (Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis is also a differential, but Perthes is statistically more common for this age/presentation).

Explanation: A 7-year-old male with a limp, left knee pain (referred pain from the hip), and no fever is highly suggestive of Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. While the patient's previous note mentioned "Migraine," that is clinically inconsistent with the physical findings of a limp and localized joint pain, so I am disregarding that claim as a misdiagnosis or error.

REQUEST IMAGES: Left Hip X-Ray (AP and Lateral views) to evaluate for femoral head fragmentation or sclerosis.
